title: Why do many U.S. neighborhoods have fire hydrants on the sidewalk?
sources: American Water Works Association Hydrant Manual

lines.text: Why are cast-iron fire hydrants positioned every few hundred feet along American sidewalks?
lines.caps: Why are fire *hydrants | placed on every *sidewalk?

lines.text: What you see above ground is just the tip of an iceberg.
lines.caps: What you see is just the *tip | of an underground *iceberg!

lines.text: Beneath the pavement sits a massive dry barrel tube extending eight feet down into the earth.
lines.caps: A dry barrel tube extends *eight feet | down into the *earth

lines.text: In cold northern states, water is kept below the frost line to prevent freezing and bursting during freezing winters.
lines.caps: Keeps water below the *frost line | so pipes never *freeze

lines.text: When firefighters crank open the top nut, a valve opens at the bottom, releasing pressurized water at thousands of gallons per minute.
lines.caps: Opening the nut releases *thousands | of gallons per *minute!

lines.text: Hydrants are color-coded: blue tops pump the highest flow over fifteen hundred gallons, while red pumps under five hundred.
lines.caps: Color-coded tops show *firefighters | the exact water *pressure

lines.text: That humble curb fixture provides instant life-saving firefighting power when every second counts.
